Dependency firewall

Usage: byrle <COMMAND>

Commands:
  daemon    Run the proxy in the foreground
  doctor    Check whether this machine installs through the proxy
  status    What this build does for each ecosystem, and which streams cover it
  explain   Why a package is allowed or refused
  audit     Work with the audit log
  intel     Read what the intel store records
  policy    Work with policy files
  lockfile  Work with lockfiles
  warm      Ask a running proxy for every artifact a lockfile locks, so each is analysed before a client asks for it. The exit code is the OR of 1 for a failure and 2 for an artifact still being analysed, and 4 on its own for an error
  refresh   Load OSV, GitHub, CISA KEV and Datadog intel into the Postgres at BYRLE_DATABASE_URL
  account   Create, list and disable accounts; set passwords; link OIDC identities
  token     Create, list and revoke the proxy tokens that identify an account on each request
  artifact  Print what each artifact was decided on, and what was decided
  help      Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -h, --help     Print help
  -V, --version  Print version

Proxy configuration, all through the environment:

  BYRLE_LISTEN                      address to listen on (default 127.0.0.1:8080)
  BYRLE_UPSTREAM_NPM                npm registry to forward to (default https://registry.npmjs.org)
  BYRLE_UPSTREAM_PYPI               PyPI simple index to forward to (default https://pypi.org/simple)
  BYRLE_PROXY_URL                   URL package managers use for the proxy. Its path is
                                    where the proxy answers, and it is written into artifact
                                    URLs, and therefore into lockfiles. Defaults to each
                                    request's own Host at /, which is rarely what you want.
  BYRLE_CONSOLE_URL                 URL of the admin console. Its path is where the console
                                    answers, and is never the proxy's. Unset, there is no console
  BYRLE_CONSOLE_LISTEN              address the console listens on. Unset, it shares
                                    BYRLE_LISTEN, and neither path may contain the other
  BYRLE_RP_KEY                      key nginx sends as X-Byrle-RP-Key, at least 32
                                    bytes. With it, X-Forwarded-For names the client.
                                    Make one with `openssl rand -hex 32`
  BYRLE_OIDC_ISSUER                 the OIDC provider console logins may use, https or
                                    loopback. With BYRLE_OIDC_CLIENT_ID and its secret
  BYRLE_OIDC_CLIENT_ID              this console's client id at BYRLE_OIDC_ISSUER
  BYRLE_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET          this console's client secret at BYRLE_OIDC_ISSUER
  BYRLE_OIDC_ALGORITHMS             algorithms an ID token may be signed with, by
                                    comma; no shared-secret one such as HS256 (default RS256,ES256)
  BYRLE_OIDC_LEEWAY_SECONDS         seconds past its exp an ID token is still taken (default 60)
  BYRLE_PASSWORD_MIN_CHARS          fewest characters a console password may have (default 15)
  BYRLE_ARGON2_MEMORY_KIB           memory, in KiB, each new password hash takes (default 19456)
  BYRLE_ARGON2_PASSES               passes over that memory each new password hash makes (default 2)
  BYRLE_SESSION_HOURS               hours a console session lasts from login (default 8)
  BYRLE_LOGIN_WINDOW_MINUTES        minutes failed console logins are counted over (default 15)
  BYRLE_LOGIN_FAILURES_PER_ACCOUNT  failed logins to one account in the window before
                                    more are refused unchecked (default 5)
  BYRLE_LOGIN_FAILURES_PER_ADDRESS  failed logins from one address, or IPv6 /64, in the
                                    window before more are refused unchecked (default 20)
  BYRLE_REQUIRE_TOKEN=0             answer requests that carry no proxy token. Unset, each
                                    request needs one, and BYRLE_DATABASE_URL is required,
                                    since accounts and tokens are kept there
  BYRLE_TOKEN                       proxy token `byrle warm` sends, from `byrle token create`
  BYRLE_ARTIFACT_ORIGINS            comma-separated origins this proxy also serves
  BYRLE_ALLOW_DIRECT_ORIGINS        comma-separated origins the proxy does not serve and
                                    permits anyway, fetched directly and unexamined
  BYRLE_REWRITE_ARTIFACTS=0         do not point artifact URLs at the proxy. pnpm and
                                    yarn then fetch artifacts without the proxy seeing
                                    them.
  BYRLE_CA_BUNDLE                   PEM bundle for the upstream connection
  BYRLE_CA_BUNDLE_EXCLUSIVE=1       trust only that bundle, not the public roots
  BYRLE_MAX_METADATA_BYTES          ceiling on a metadata document (default 64 MiB)
  BYRLE_MAX_RECORDS                 package records held in memory (default 50000)
  BYRLE_MAX_VERIFIED                verified artifact digests remembered (default 50000)
  BYRLE_PROVENANCE_HISTORY          attested versions older than provenance_window_days
                                    a version's identity is looked for in, most recent first (default 64)
  BYRLE_DATABASE_URL                Postgres holding intel from `byrle refresh`. With a
                                    policy, known_malware is enforced from it, and a
                                    store that cannot answer is a 503
  BYRLE_STREAM_URLS                 stream=url pairs, by comma, fetching a stream from a
                                    mirror: osv/npm=https://mirror.example/npm/all.zip.
                                    https, or http to loopback; others keep their own
  BYRLE_GITHUB_TOKEN                token `byrle refresh` reads GitHub's Advisory
                                    Database with. Unset, that one stream does not load
                                    and the others still do
  BYRLE_SNAPSHOT_DIR                directory `byrle refresh` keeps each snapshot in,
                                    for `policy diff --snapshot`. Unset, none is kept
  BYRLE_SNAPSHOT_LIMIT              most snapshots kept there; a refresh removes older ones (default 30)
  BYRLE_POLICY                      path to a policy file. Loaded, validated and
                                    enforced. Startup reports which checks can fire
  BYRLE_AUDIT_LOG                   path for one JSON line per policy decision,
                                    appended. Renamed with its date at UTC midnight;
                                    files 3 days old and older are compressed with
                                    bzip2. Refuses to start if it cannot be opened
  BYRLE_ACCOUNT_EVENT_LOG           path for one JSON line per change to an account,
                                    its roles, tokens or password, and per console
                                    login and logout. Rotated as BYRLE_AUDIT_LOG is
  BYRLE_LOG_RETENTION_DAYS          days a rotated audit or account event log file is kept (default 365)
  BYRLE_DECISION_RETENTION_DAYS     days an artifact decision is kept in the analysis store (default 365)
  BYRLE_EXPIRY_CEILING_DAYS         how many days ahead a `packages` entry may be dated (default 90)
  BYRLE_MAX_CONCURRENT_METADATA     metadata documents decoded at once (default 8)
  BYRLE_SPOOL_DIR                   directory an artifact is written to while it is
                                    analysed. Locked; spool files left in it are removed
                                    at startup (default byrle-spool in the OS temp dir)
  BYRLE_MAX_ARTIFACT_BYTES          ceiling on an artifact written to the spool (default 1024 MiB)
  BYRLE_MAX_CONCURRENT_ANALYSES     artifacts analysed at once (default 8)
  BYRLE_MAX_TRAFFIC_CLIENTS         client names counted apart in a traffic window (default 256)
  BYRLE_WATCH_INTERVAL              seconds between checks of served packages for new versions to analyse
                                    before a client asks for them; 0 turns it off (default 900)
  BYRLE_SOURCE_ARCHIVES             host of the GitHub archives each artifact is compared with, the source
                                    its metadata names; off turns the comparison off (default https://codeload.github.com)
  BYRLE_DETECTORS                   detectors run on each version served, `name=command argument...`, separated by `;`;
                                    {ecosystem}, {name} and {version} in the arguments are replaced. A detector is given
                                    PATH, HOME, SOCKS and the forward proxies, and nothing else
  BYRLE_VIRUSTOTAL_API_KEY          key each artifact's SHA-256 is looked up on VirusTotal with, a report-only
                                    signal. Unset, VirusTotal is not asked
  BYRLE_VIRUSTOTAL_MODE             "upload" also sends VirusTotal an artifact it does not know, when it came from
                                    a public registry (default hash)
  BYRLE_VIRUSTOTAL_URL              VirusTotal's API (default https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3)
  BYRLE_VIRUSTOTAL_PER_MINUTE       requests to VirusTotal a minute; the public API allows 4 (default 4)
  BYRLE_VIRUSTOTAL_PER_DAY          requests to VirusTotal a day; the public API allows 500 (default 500)
  BYRLE_REFUSAL_STATUS              status a refusal answers with, per client, e.g.
                                    "default=403,npm/pnpm=451" (default 403)
  BYRLE_REFUSE_UNSERVABLE=0         forward versions whose artifacts this proxy cannot
                                    see, instead of removing them from the metadata
  BYRLE_MODE                        "observe" serves what the policy refuses and logs it (default enforce)
  HTTPS_PROXY                       forward proxy for upstream https; the lowercase name
                                    is read too
  HTTP_PROXY                        forward proxy for upstream http; the lowercase name
                                    is read too
  NO_PROXY                          hosts fetched without the forward proxy, comma-separated;
                                    the lowercase name is read too
  BYRLE_LOG_FORMAT                  "json" writes one OpenTelemetry log record per line (default text)
  RUST_LOG                          log filter, in tracing's syntax (default byrle=info)
  BYRLE_DEFER_TEST                  DEBUG BUILDS ONLY: answer every matching request with
                                    a deferral instead of fetching, so client retry
                                    behaviour can be measured. `<status>:<seconds|none>:
                                    <metadata|artifact|all>[:<seconds>]`, e.g.
                                    "429:1:artifact" or "503:1:all:8"
